title: A record number of workers — but what about the rate?
claim: More Americans are working today than at any time in the history of our country
summary: The number employed reached a record as the population grew; the employment-to-population ratio was below its January 2025 level.

title: Zero illegal entries? That is not what the data show.
claim: In the past 17 months, zero illegal aliens have been admitted to the United States
summary: The administration reported zero releases at the southern border, not zero attempts or successful unauthorized crossings.

title: A 97% drop in ocean drug trafficking? Show the data.
claim: We brought the flow of deadly drugs coming in by ocean down by 97%
summary: There is no comprehensive measure of all drugs trafficked by sea, including shipments that were not seized.

title: No tax on tips, overtime or Social Security? Terms apply.
claim: No tax on tips, no tax on overtime, no tax on Social Security
summary: The deductions have caps and income restrictions; the Social Security provision does not eliminate all taxes on benefits.

title: Five-thousand-dollar checks and tariff arithmetic
claim: Tariff revenue would help pay $5,000 to every adult citizen
summary: Paying eligible adults would cost around $1.2 trillion, far above a year's tariff receipts.

title: Greatest economy in history? GDP tells a different story.
claim: We had the greatest economy in the history of our country
summary: Real GDP growth during Trump's first term was exceeded in many earlier years.

title: The $21 trillion investment claim
claim: We have $21 trillion being invested in our country
summary: No full accounting substantiates the figure, and announced commitments are not equivalent to completed investment.

title: Worst inflation in U.S. history? No.
claim: I inherited the worst inflation in American history
summary: Inflation was 3.0% when Trump took office in January 2025; historical peaks were much higher.

title: Record-low poverty — which measure?
claim: The poverty rate has just reached its lowest level
summary: The official poverty rate reached a low in 2025, but the supplemental poverty measure did not.

title: The $20 trillion foreign-investment assertion
claim: An unprecedented $20 trillion has been invested in the U.S. from outside countries and companies
summary: FactCheck.org found no evidence substantiating this total.

title: Election security speech: insinuation is not evidence
claim: References to a 'stolen election' and supposed hidden vulnerabilities
summary: FactCheck.org found that Trump's speech provided no evidence of widespread fraud and offered little new information about election vulnerabilities.

title: A perfect cognitive-screening score is not an IQ score
claim: I scored a perfect 30 out of 30, considered ‘extreme intelligence.’
summary: Trump reported a 30/30 score on the Montreal Cognitive Assessment. Its creator and medical experts explain that MoCA screens for cognitive impairment; it does not measure IQ or establish 'extreme intelligence'. Trump described this as his fourth perfect test, so it is inaccurate to say he had taken only one test.

title: Inflation had 'stopped'? Prices kept rising.
claim: Inflation was the worst in history when he took office, and had now stopped
summary: FactCheck.org found both the historical comparison and the suggestion that inflation had stopped inaccurate.

title: Tylenol and autism: causation was not established
claim: Trump suggested a link between acetaminophen use in pregnancy and autism
summary: A causal link has not been established.

title: Were U.S. jobs numbers 'rigged'?
claim: The Bureau of Labor Statistics employment figures were phony or rigged
summary: No evidence of political manipulation was found; routine revisions are normal.

title: The 'reciprocal tariffs' chart wasn't showing foreign tariff rates
claim: The chart showed the tariffs other countries charge the United States
summary: The displayed figures were based on trade deficits, not actual foreign tariff rates.

title: DOGE found hundreds of billions in fraud?
claim: DOGE has found hundreds of billions of dollars of fraud
summary: DOGE claimed much less in savings and documented only a fraction; savings are not proven fraud.

title: Panama, not China, controls the canal
claim: China is operating the Panama Canal
summary: Panama operates the canal; Hong Kong-based firms managed some nearby ports.

title: Did Pelosi reject 10,000 National Guard troops?
claim: Nancy Pelosi rejected 10,000 National Guard troops before January 6
summary: Pelosi did not control the Guard, and no presidential order for 10,000 troops was issued.

title: A pardon and a commutation are not the same
claim: Biden pardoned 33 murderers
summary: Biden commuted 37 death sentences, not pardoned 33 people.

title: Claims at the Harris–Trump debate
claim: False and misleading statements about the 2020 election and January 6
summary: FactCheck.org examined multiple disputed claims about the Capitol attack and election results in the debate. This entry is a topic overview.

title: Abortions 'after birth'? That would be homicide.
claim: Some states allow abortions after birth
summary: FactCheck.org notes that killing a baby after birth is homicide and illegal; the claim misrepresents abortion law.

title: The debt payoff that never had a budget
claim: We would have started paying down the debt by selling energy abroad
summary: FactCheck.org found the claim unsupported; public debt rose during Trump's first term.

title: Wind turbines 'don't work'? The grid disagrees.
claim: Windmills don't work
summary: FactCheck.org found the assertion about wind energy false and also examined Trump's claims about manufacturing origins.

title: The Georgia call, remembered differently
claim: I didn't ask Georgia's secretary of state to find me more votes
summary: A recorded 2021 call documents Trump asking Brad Raffensperger to find 11,780 votes.

title: The FBI 'staged' the Mar-a-Lago photograph?
claim: The FBI staged a photo of seized classified documents
summary: Agents arranged seized materials for an evidentiary photograph; that did not mean the documents were fabricated.

title: Election fraud claims despite aides' warnings
claim: Assertions of widespread 2020 election fraud
summary: Testimony at the Jan. 6 committee documented that aides told Trump his election fraud allegations were baseless.

title: Gasoline wasn't $1.86 nationally when Trump left office
claim: Gas prices were $1.86 when I left the White House
summary: PolitiFact reported a national average of roughly $2.38 per gallon.

title: Was Trump 'right about everything'?
claim: I was right about everything
summary: PolitiFact found accurate claims, unsupported assertions and opinion, not a uniformly correct record.

title: Georgia's 66,000 underage voters? Officials said zero.
claim: 66,000 votes in Georgia were cast by individuals under the legal voting age
summary: Georgia's Republican election officials said the actual number was zero.

title: Declaring victory before votes were counted
claim: Frankly, we did win this election
summary: Trump declared victory before all ballots had been counted; later certified results showed Biden won.

title: Acing a cognitive screen isn't acing an intelligence test
claim: I proved I was all there, because I aced it. I aced the test.
summary: Trump said he aced a cognitive assessment. Such screening assesses cognitive functioning rather than IQ; a high score alone cannot establish exceptional intelligence.
statementVenue: Fox News interview with Sean Hannity

title: Wind turbine noise causes cancer? Evidence says no.
claim: They say the noise causes cancer
summary: FactCheck.org and the American Cancer Society found no credible evidence that wind turbine noise causes cancer.

title: DACA for new border arrivals? That's not how it works.
claim: Big flows of people are coming to take advantage of DACA
summary: DACA eligibility does not extend to people newly crossing the border.

title: The 'very stable genius' declaration
claim: I think that would qualify as not smart, but genius....and a very stable genius at that!
summary: Trump publicly described himself as a 'very stable genius'. The phrase is an opinion about himself, not a measurable factual finding. His later MoCA screening results cannot validate a claim about IQ.

sources.label: PolitiFact — IQ claim and test context

title: The first-month national-debt drop: true number, wrong implication
claim: The national debt in my first month went down by $12 billion
summary: The temporary drop reflected federal cash flows, not a lasting debt reduction.

title: Inauguration crowds: photos versus the claim
claim: The crowd looked like a million-and-a-half people
summary: Contemporaneous photographs and transit figures contradict claims that the crowd reached the Washington Monument or exceeded the 2009 inauguration.

title: The 'sex tape' tweet he said he never sent
claim: There wasn't 'check out a sex tape'
summary: FactCheck.org documented Trump's September 30 tweet using the very phrase he denied during the October 9 debate.
statementVenue: Second presidential debate, Washington University, St. Louis, Missouri

title: Tax returns: from 'certainly' to audit excuses
claim: He couldn't release tax returns while being audited
summary: FactCheck.org documented Trump's reversal on releasing returns and explained that an audit did not prevent publication.

title: Thousands cheering in New Jersey on 9/11?
claim: I watched in Jersey City, N.J., where thousands and thousands of people were cheering
summary: Independent investigations found no evidence for the thousands-strong celebrations in New Jersey described by Trump.
